elements.quote: All English-language published studies identified in our systematic search (up to February 3, 2021) examining the use of MSC-derived products to treat patients with COVID-19 were identified.
elements.reason: The abstract mentions a 'systematic search' and RoB assessment, but does not explicitly label the report as a systematic review within the abstract text.

elements.quote: Methods and Findings: All English-language published studies identified in our systematic search (up to February 3, 2021) examining the use of MSC-derived products to treat patients with COVID-19 were identified.
elements.reason: The abstract's Methods and Findings and Conclusion sections do not contain an explicit statement of the objective or review question.

elements.quote: All English-language published studies identified in our systematic search (up to February 3, 2021) examining the use of MSC-derived products to treat patients with COVID-19 were identified.
elements.reason: The abstract states the eligibility criteria: English-language published studies of MSC-derived products to treat COVID-19 patients.

elements.quote: identified in our systematic search (up to February 3, 2021)
elements.reason: The abstract reports the search end date but does not name the information sources (databases) searched.

elements.quote: Risk of bias (RoB) was assessed for all studies.
elements.reason: The abstract states that risk of bias was assessed but does not describe the methods/tools used.

elements.quote: Three of the controlled studies reported on mortality (primary analysis) and were pooled through random-effects meta-analysis.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the synthesis methods, i.e., random-effects meta-analysis, with other outcomes not pooled.

elements.quote: Nine studies were identified (189 patients), four of which were controlled (93 patients).
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies and participants, with study characteristics (controlled vs uncontrolled).

elements.quote: MSCs decreased the risk of death at study endpoint compared with controls (risk ratio, 0.18; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.04 to 0.74; P = .02; I 2 = 0%)
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcome (mortality) and a key secondary outcome (IL-6), including effect estimates.

elements.quote: risk ratio, 0.18; 95% con fi dence interval [CI], 0.04 to 0.74; P = .02; I 2 = 0%
elements.reason: The meta-analysis summary estimate and its 95% CI are reported for mortality and for IL-6 (SMD, -0.69; 95% CI, -1.15 to -0.22).

elements.quote: MSCs decreased the risk of death at study endpoint compared with controls
elements.reason: The abstract clearly indicates the direction of effect, favoring the MSC group over controls.

elements.quote: however, few studies were identi fi ed, and potential risk of bias was detected in all studies.
elements.reason: The abstract summarizes important limitations: few studies, risk of bias, and substantial heterogeneity in study design.

elements.quote: Conclusion: Use of MSCs to treat COVID-19 appears promising; however, few studies were identi fi ed, and potential risk of bias was detected in all studies.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their implications, including recommendations for future research.
No statement of the primary funding source appears in the abstract.
Although registration (PROSPERO; CRD42021225431) is reported in the Methods section (text_7), it is not provided in the abstract.

elements.quote: Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) and their secreted products are a promising therapy for COVID-19 given their immunomodulatory and tissue repair capabilities. Many small studies were launched at the onset of the pandemic
elements.reason: The abstract background indicates current knowledge (promising therapy, many small studies) and implies uncertainty about efficacy, but the full Introduction section with a detailed account of existing knowledge and uncertainties was not retrieved.

elements.quote: repeated meta-analysis is critical to obtain timely and sufficient statistical power to determine efficacy
elements.reason: The need for the review is explicitly stated: repeated meta-analysis is needed for timely, adequately powered estimation of efficacy.

elements.quote: many registered clinical trials dealing with the use of MSC-based products as a therapeutic intervention for COVID-19 were identified in a scoping review performed by our group [31]
elements.reason: Although described as the first iteration of a living review and a prior scoping review is mentioned, the manuscript does not explicitly discuss or cite previous similar systematic reviews to justify the need for this review.

elements.quote: Thus, the pleiotropic anti-inflammatory and regenerative effects of MSCs may point to several potential mechanisms by which MSCs exert their apparent beneficial effect.
elements.reason: Mechanisms of action (immunomodulation via cytokine modulation, macrophage repolarization, tissue regeneration; see also Table 7) are described in detail.
No logic model showing hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes is reported; only a narrative mechanism table is provided.

No retrieved evidence contains an explicit statement of the review objective(s) or question(s) using a question-formulation framework. The abstract background (text_4) only describes motivation, and Methods sections discuss search, selection, and analysis without stating formal objectives.

This is a review of intervention effects (MSC therapy for COVID-19), so planned comparisons are relevant; however, no PICO-formulated statement of comparisons appears in the retrieved evidence. Comparisons (e.g., control vs experimental) are only implied within the Data Analysis text (text_13), not stated as planned PICO-based comparisons.

elements.quote: Specific data extracted from studies included study characteristics (e.g., authors, publication year, country of study), study design (characteristics of control group, sample size, length of observation period, planned preconditioning or alterations to MSCs or secreted factors before therapeutic use, MSC/secretome isolation and characterization methods, etc.), patient characteristics (age, sex, comorbidities, COVID-19 severity, symptoms upon hospital admission, etc.), intervention characteristics (MSC tissue source, MSC/secretome dose, route of administration, number of doses, whether MSC-based products met all of the minimal criteria established in guidelines by the International Society for Cellular Therapy [ISCT] [35] and/or Minimal Information for Studies of Extracellular Vesicles [MISEV] [36] criteria), all data pertaining to primary and secondary outcomes, and details concerning risk of bias (RoB) determination.
elements.reason: The Data Extraction section comprehensively lists and defines the study, patient, intervention, outcome, and risk-of-bias variables for which data were sought, including funding-relevant characteristics such as product characterization standards.

elements.quote: using a standardized data extraction template in Microsoft Excel (Microsoft, Seattle, WA)

elements.quote: All relevant data was extracted in duplicate by two independent reviewers (A.M. Kirkham, M. Monaghan) from the included studies... and details concerning risk of bias (RoB) determination.

elements.quote: For dichotomous outcomes, risk ratios (RRs) were calculated... For continuous outcomes, the standardized mean difference (SMD) between control and experimental groups was calculated using random effects meta-analyses.

elements.quote: Meta-analysis was performed only when three or more controlled studies reported on the same outcome. Outcomes that were reported in fewer than three controlled studies or for which adequate data for inclusion in meta-analysis was not provided were analyzed in a descriptive manner.
